items.summary: NVIDIA introduced ExecuTorch-TensorRT, a workflow that lets developers compile PyTorch robot policies with Torch-TensorRT 2.15 and run them as ExecuTorch 1.6 programs without loading the torch library on edge devices like robots. The approach compiles models directly through PyTorch's torch.export into TensorRT engines while routing any unsupported operations—such as preprocessing or ops like erfinv—to ExecuTorch's CUDA backend, which runs those parts on the GPU in the same program and stream instead of failing the build; if a custom op is needed, it can be written as a Triton kernel without requiring C++ plugins. On an 8 GB NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super (about $250), ExecuTorch-TensorRT ran four robot policies from LeRobot—ACT, SmolVLA, pi0.5, and GR00T 1.7 (3B)—within 4% of the fastest ONNX-TensorRT setup in both speed and memory while running about up to 6.4x faster than PyTorch eager mode; a 3.6-billion-parameter policy fit on the board where PyTorch eager mode ran out of memory, completing a chunk of 50 actions for pi0.5 in roughly half a second versus PyTorch's failure. The team presented this work at PyTorch Conference 2026 under 'Deploying Robot Policies Across Many Targets with ExecuTorch.' Installation requires one pip install command (torch_tensorrt[executorch]), built for CUDA 13.2 on Linux, x86-64 and Arm64, targeting JetPack 7.2 or newer; the first Arm64 install pulls about 2.6 GB of TensorRT libraries because Torch-TensorRT 2.15 needs TensorRT 11.4 while JetPack 7.2 ships with version 10. For running on robots without PyTorch, ExecuTorch 1.6's Python runtime no longer requires the torch library and handles NumPy arrays in and out; importing PyTorch alone takes about 2.2 s and 550 MB on the Orin Nano versus a smaller install of roughly 4.6 GB for just the runtime, TensorRT backend, and needed libraries instead of 11 GB for the full setup. The workflow also supports running in C++ by linking provided CMake packages, with GPU-resident inputs like camera frames allowing direct pointer passing to skip CPU copies.
items.title: ExecuTorch-TensorRT: PyTorch Robot Policies at NVIDIA TensorRT Speed

items.summary: NVIDIA has released a streaming adapter in the Cosmos-Framework package that lets users run the Cosmos 3 Nano video-generation model locally on consumer GPUs with as little as 12 GB of VRAM, according to the tutorial. The approach stores most model weights in system RAM and transfers them to the GPU only when needed while keeping all matrix multiplication and attention operations on CUDA; it builds on Hugging Face Diffusers' native group offloading but requires increased system RAM use and PCIe transfers during generation rather than interactive latency or streaming directly from disk, per NVIDIA. The tested consumer-GPU hosts had approximately 128 GB of system RAM, though that figure is not a measured minimum for the method. Users install the standalone offloading package via uv pip in an environment with Python 3.12 and a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build compatible with their GPU, then pass the Hugging Face repository ID to build_pipeline; the first load downloads the checkpoint while subsequent loads reuse cached files, with safety checking enabled by default. The baseline example uses BF16 precision with PyTorch scaled dot-product attention across four tested GPUs and generates 189 frames at 720p (with suggested smaller resolutions of 480x848 or 240x432 for faster iteration on a 12 GB GPU). The adapter manages memory in four ways: keeping unused checkpoint weights in system RAM as BF16 or FP8, transferring the next transformer block to the GPU when required, running every matrix multiplication and attention operation on CUDA, and managing denoising, VAE encode/decode, and safety-checking memory. NVIDIA Cosmos 3 has two complementary pathways inside its transformer: an understanding pathway that interprets fixed conditioning inputs once and reuses their context during generation, and a generation pathway that processes the evolving video, sound, or action representation at every denoising step using that context. A 35-step request runs through 36 transformer blocks (indexed 0 through 35), with the scheduler updating state between steps; classifier-free guidance reuses each streamed block across its prediction branches rather than transferring weights for each branch. The adapter automatically reuses fixed understanding work, streams generation blocks from system RAM to GPU as needed, overlaps transfers with computation when headroom allows (with larger workloads falling back to a safer lower-memory schedule), and manages VAE decoding and safety checks separately using memory-efficient execution on constrained cards; users do not configure device-specific tuning values. The tutorial also covers image-to-video conditioning, video-to-video generation selecting condition frames, generating sound with an audio description alongside video, combining image input with sound output, CosmosActionCondition for action domains at 480p resolution tier producing 17 frames over 30 steps (outputting 640x480 rather than 1280x720), and control-video guidance. For the FP8 checkpoint, users install the fp8 extra including NVIDIA Model Optimizer and select revision='fp8' with checkpoint_precision='fp8'; W8A16 reuses stored 8-bit weights dequantized for linear operations with 16-bit activations while W8A8 uses 8-bit weights and activations, though attention remains BF16 SDPA so the entire pipeline does not run in FP8. The presented results cover text-to-video across four GeForce RTX cards and all seven generation modalities on the GeForce RTX 5070 at 12 GB VRAM with a 128 GB-class host; Table 4 compares text-to-video measurements while Table 5 lists full generations excluding checkpoint loading and MP4 encoding, with times in pipeline-call seconds and peaks reported as device-used GPU memory in GiB. NVIDIA notes these are guidance ranges rather than fixed limits because resolution, frame count, modality, checkpoint precision, available system RAM, and PCIe bandwidth all affect fit and runtime, and that single-run measurements can be affected by host configuration and safety settings so they do not represent a controlled GPU ranking or multiseed BF16-versus-FP8 comparison. The tutorial directs users to download the Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoint and its FP8 branch on Hugging Face, find examples in the Cosmos-Framework offloading package, review Diffusers' memory optimization guide for CPU offloading, and join the community through GitHub and Discord.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Cosmos-Framework Adapter to Run Cosmos 3 Nano on GPUs with as Little as 12 GB VRAM

items.summary: Technology shares led a market retreat on Tuesday, with caution returning after CEO Jensen Huang was reinstated at Nvidia just days after being forced to resign. The euphoria from his return dissipated quickly: following a session in which Nvidia shares rose more than 30%—adding over $900bn to the company's market value—a subsequent mid-session decline saw its stock fall almost 9%. Anthropic also slumped, giving up about 12% to $77.19, below its $83 price for last week's IPO. Monday aside, AI stocks had already sold off sharply throughout November amid worries about profitability and the vast sums being pumped into the sector. By noon in New York, the tech-heavy Nasdaq had shed 2.3%, while the broader S&P 500 lost 1.1%; the Dow was just entering green territory. Europe's main stock markets—featuring far fewer tech companies than their Asian and US counterparts—finished a handful of percentage points lower after jumping Monday in line with Wall Street. Huang had resigned less than two weeks earlier over extramarital affairs, reportedly involving an alleged Chinese spy as well as a senior Nvidia executive, before Donald Trump declared he should be brought back. Charu Chanana, an investment strategist at Saxo Markets, said "Jensen's return takes away one of the biggest unknowns hanging over the AI trade," noting that Huang is not just Nvidia's CEO but arguably the biggest salesman for the entire AI ecosystem and that his relationships with customers, suppliers, and capital providers are difficult to replicate. However, Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, cautioned that "Jensen Huang alone cannot support the AI trade in the long term" and described Tuesday's Nvidia decline as expected after such a large rally the previous session. Analysts broadly agreed that Huang's return did not signal an end to investigations or the uncertainty that has clouded the AI trade for six months; Nvidia remains under scrutiny from investigators including at the FBI and on Capitol Hill over allegations it helped Chinese firms gain access to its top-line chips.
items.title: Tech Sell-off Resumes as Nvidia Euphoria Subsides After Jensen Huang's Return

visual.alt: Bar chart. Nvidia (mid-session decline) 9 %; Anthropic (decline vs IPO price) 12 %; Nasdaq (by noon, NY time) 2.3 %; S&P 500 (decline) 1.1 %.

items.summary: An Amazon delivery drone that clipped a fiber-optic line before crashing onto a garage roof is now the subject of an investigation by the US Federal Aviation Administration. The November 20 incident began with Jim Brennan and his wife, residents of Huntington Woods, Michigan, placing an order for shampoo and receiving a notification about the package arriving by drone within seven minutes, according to WXYZ 7 News Detroit. After the drone dropped the package into Brennan's backyard, it lost a propeller when it caught on fiber-optic cable and floundered sideways before getting pinned between the neighbor's garage roof and some power lines. Amazon Prime Air currently operates a fleet of battery-powered MK30 drones that can deliver packages weighing up to five pounds and have onboard sense-and-avoid technology to avoid obstacles, though this drone failed to avoid the thin fiber-optic cable in this case. The FAA preliminary accident and incident notification briefly describes the incident as 'UAS struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff,' posted on November 23. The National Transportation Safety Board is also gathering information about the incident but has not yet decided whether to open its own probe, according to CNBC.
items.title: Amazon Drone Crashes on Garage After Delivering Shampoo, Draws FAA Probe

items.summary: Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's headquarters on Monday with a hero's welcome, hours after being reinstated as chief executive of the world's most valuable chip company following an intervention by Donald Trump. The reversal occurred less than two weeks after Huang resigned from the role amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving an alleged Chinese spy and two employees at Nvidia. As the dominant supplier of semiconductors for building and operating AI systems, Nvidia became the subject of a staff survey asking employees what they think of the decision to reinstate Huang as chief executive, whether it says something about the company and the state of the AI sector, and any concerns they may have.
items.title: Jensen Huang Reinstated as Nvidia Chief Executive After Trump Intervention

items.summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned as chief executive on November 23, just 11 days after resigning, following support from employees, investors and US President Donald Trump. The announcement drove Nvidia shares up 31%, helping the Nasdaq gain 6.5%. The rally extended to Asian markets: South Korea's Kospi rose 6.3%, Japan's Nikkei gained 4% and Taiwan's Taiex advanced 9%. Huang's reinstatement has renewed discussion about founder influence, board independence and what prompts companies to recall former leaders.

The article frames the return within a broader history of executives returning during financial distress or leadership crises. Steve Jobs left Apple in 1985 after a boardroom dispute and returned more than a decade later following Apple's acquisition of NeXT; his subsequent leadership delivered the iMac, iPod and iPhone. Infosys' Murthy came back as executive chairman seven years after stepping away from an executive role while the company reported revenue growth of just 5.8% in FY13.

Howard Schultz returned to Starbucks twice: first in 2008 amid slowing sales and concerns over aggressive expansion, then again in 2022 as interim CEO during leadership uncertainty and growing unionisation efforts. Jack Dorsey was removed from Twitter's CEO role in 2008 and returned seven years later following Dick Costolo's departure; his simultaneous leadership of Twitter and Square drew scrutiny from activist investors.

Bob Iger came back less than three years after handing leadership to Bob Chapek, when mounting streaming losses, disappointing financial performance and strategic concerns prompted Disney's board to reverse its succession decision. Pat Gelsinger returned to Intel after nearly 12 years to restore technological competitiveness; his ambitious manufacturing strategy faced challenges, and his departure in December 2024 illustrated that recalling experienced executives does not guarantee a turnaround.

Elliott Hill came back four years after retiring as Nike's CEO for the first time, with the company seeking his institutional knowledge to rebuild retailer relationships and revive consumer demand. Sam Altman returned to OpenAI just five days after dismissal; more than 700 employees threatened to resign unless he was reinstated while Microsoft offered him a leadership role, and OpenAI subsequently reconstituted its board.

Huang's case adds political influence as another governance dimension: Trump claimed he had personally persuaded Nvidia's board to bring Huang back. When asked whether Huang would have returned without his involvement, Trump told CNBC "The answer is no," adding that "I believe my intervention was very important." Nvidia confirmed receiving input from senior US government officials before unanimously approving the reinstatement. Trump's disclosed Nvidia investments raised potential conflict-of-interest questions, though the White House maintains third-party institutions manage his accounts.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Return to Nvidia Joins a Lineage of Corporate Comebacks

visual.alt: Bar chart. Nvidia shares (Huang return) 31 %; Nasdaq gain 6.5 %; Kospi rise 6.3 %; Nikkei gain 4 %; Taiex advance 9 %; Infosys FY13 revenue growth 5.8 %.

items.summary: On Tuesday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff via livestream reviewed by the New York Times, saying "I made some terrible mistakes" and that he was unfaithful to his wife Lori. The apology came one day after the board reinstated him on Monday—less than two weeks after he had been ousted—and less than a week after admitting to violating Nvidia's code of conduct for having extramarital affairs with at least two company employees, according to news reports that also allege relationships involving a suspected Chinese spy. Huang said during Tuesday's address that he was in therapy and called his actions "not acceptable." He pushed back on reporting that Donald Trump pressured the board into reinstating him, calling it "completely untrue," while acknowledging Trump assured the board he posed no national security threat; Semafor reported that Trump dialed into Nvidia's Sunday board meeting to advocate for Huang's return. The US government is investigating whether Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company formerly run by Alice Huang—Huang's alleged ex-lover and not related to him—diverted Nvidia semiconductors to China in breach of export controls, with officials also raising concerns about her alleged role as a Chinese asset. Huang faces two congressional hearings next week before the House Foreign Affairs Committee and Senate Banking committee; Gregory Meeks, ranking member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said on Tuesday that a hearing should still take place so the American people can learn how potentially billions of dollars in advanced technology reached China and what role this administration played. Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
items.title: Jensen Huang Apologizes After Nvidia Board Reinstates Him as CEO

items.summary: Andy Burnham is facing a backlash for inviting social media influencers to Downing Street, following an incident in which one attendee posted a clip of himself miming explicit lyrics outside No 10. Max Balegde was given the invitation as part of Burnham's efforts to engage with online celebrities and posted a TikTok video mouthing the words 'bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets' — bomboclaat being a Jamaican profanity referring to a menstrual cloth — after attending an event at the prime minister's residence. Downing Street said it was right that Balegde had taken down the post, with a spokesperson stating: 'It is right the creator took down that content.' The PM's spokesperson added that creators are responsible for what they choose to post and defended holding the reception on 9 November, arguing the influencers attending had a combined audience of more than 470 million. Videos from the evening have since emerged online, including one showing Luke Hamnett recreating Hugh Grant's prime ministerial dance from Love Actually inside No 10.
items.title: Burnham under fire over influencers' No 10 reception after TikTok video row

items.summary: Republicans in the US Congress have broken ranks with President Donald Trump, joining Democrats in demanding an investigation into the Nvidia scandal after co-founder Jensen Huang returned to the chip-maker 11 days after resigning over alleged extramarital affairs. Mr Trump personally intervened to secure Huang's reinstatement, telling CNBC: 'I made the deal,' while claiming credit for the move despite his own financial interests being scrutinized—his Nvidia holdings were valued at between US$13 million and US$62 million as of late August, with The Financial Times calculating that a share-price rebound may have added up to US$15 million to Trump's stake on Monday. At the heart of the controversy are allegations that advanced chips were diverted to China through Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company formerly led by Alice Huang, whom US intelligence suspects works for Beijing and with whom Jensen Huang reportedly had an affair. Nvidia's board said it received input from senior US government officials and was confident Huang posed no national security risk, even though its independent investigation remained unfinished; Senator John Curtis demanded to know who provided those assurances on X, while Senate Intelligence Committee chairman Tom Cotton warned that Congress has much to investigate. The dissent represents an unusually strong show of opposition among Senate Republicans, with at least six objecting over the reinstatement—though most directed criticism at Nvidia or questioned administration assurances rather than attacking Trump personally. Huang is scheduled for closed-door questioning on December 1 before three Republican-led House committees and public testimony before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, while Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed to appear on December 10 per CBS News; Congress also faces scrutiny over its handling of Megaspeed, which was added to a trade blacklist Monday. The controversy is strengthening bipartisan calls for chip export-control legislation, with Mr Cotton promising to push ahead and Senate Republican leader John Thune pledging support, while Democrats say they are preparing to use their new congressional majorities from January to investigate potential corruption involving Nvidia and senior Trump officials.
items.title: Republican China Hawks Challenge Trump Over Jensen Huang's Nvidia Return

items.summary: In an hourlong companywide meeting on Tuesday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang denied that US President Donald Trump had pressured the board to reinstate him as president and CEO of the chipmaker. The remarks came a day after his return was announced by Nvidia's board, which unanimously reinstated him Monday following discussions with Huang and input from senior US government officials who gave the board confidence his return posed no national security risk. Huang rejected suggestions that his reinstatement resulted from political pressure or preferential treatment because of his influence in technology, telling employees via an internal livestream reviewed by The New York Times, "That is completely untrue." He also said he had not returned because he was a tech figure who was above the law or code of conduct. Trump earlier told CNBC that he had spoken with Nvidia's board and convinced its members to bring Huang back. Huang acknowledged violating Nvidia's code of conduct, which he helped write, apologized to employees for his actions, and took responsibility for an affair with his wife Lori that hurt his children and colleagues. He said the situation forced the board to evaluate his future, leading to his resignation on Nov. 11 after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang also stated he was undergoing therapy, attending sessions of about 90 minutes daily according to WIRED, which reviewed his remarks alongside The New York Times. He rejected reports describing him as an abusive boss and defended Nvidia's management structure.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Denies Trump Pressured Board to Reinstale Him
